title: getToken performs case-sensitive exact-match on address while canonical tokens are stored EIP-55 checksummed
reasoning: The D1 tokens table is populated by writeThroughD1 with addresses from the canonical Uniswap list, which the module header (lines 4-7) says is validated for EIP-55 checksums. token.service.getToken queries `WHERE address = ${address}` verbatim, so a caller passing a lowercase or otherwise differently-cased address (typical for user input from wallets/URLs) will miss a valid stored token and return null, producing a 404 for an existing token. The sibling implementation in token-list.service.ts (lines 232-237) explicitly lowercases both sides of the comparison, showing the author knew case normalization matters. The HTTP layer is not included here, so normalization may or may not happen upstream; the two services are internally inconsistent, which is a contract hazard.
reproduction: Insert a token with checksummed address 0xAbC...; call getToken('0xabc...'); observe null despite the token existing.
recommendation: Normalize in the service: e.g. query `WHERE LOWER(address) = LOWER(${address})` or normalize the input to the stored format before binding (preferable to keep index usage), and mirror the same normalization in upsertToken so stored addresses have a canonical case.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No test files were included for this feature (tests: []), and no tests are referenced by either service file.
suggestedRegressionTest: Insert a token via upsertToken with a checksummed address, then call getToken with the all-lowercase form of the same address and assert the token is returned (and vice versa).
